osc1.title: Oscillator 1
osc1.concept: An oscillator makes a wave that repeats many times a second. The repeat rate is the pitch and the wave's shape is the tone.
osc1.what: Where sound starts. It repeats one wave shape: how fast sets the pitch, the shape sets the tone.
osc1.listenFor: Play a low note, then a high one. The tone stays the same; only the pitch moves.
osc1.tryThis: Hold a note and switch between the four waves. Saw is brightest because it has every harmonic.

osc2.title: Oscillator 2
osc2.concept: An oscillator makes a wave that repeats many times a second. The repeat rate is the pitch and the wave's shape is the tone.
osc2.what: Where sound starts. It repeats one wave shape: how fast sets the pitch, the shape sets the tone. Add it to layer with other oscillators.
osc2.listenFor: Play a low note, then a high one. The tone stays the same; only the pitch moves.
osc2.tryThis: Set Fine to +7 cents against Oscillator 1 and hold a note to hear the shimmer.

osc3.title: Oscillator 3
osc3.concept: An oscillator makes a wave that repeats many times a second. The repeat rate is the pitch and the wave's shape is the tone.
osc3.what: Where sound starts. It repeats one wave shape: how fast sets the pitch, the shape sets the tone. Add it to layer with other oscillators.
osc3.listenFor: Play a low note, then a high one. The tone stays the same; only the pitch moves.
osc3.tryThis: Set Fine to +7 cents against Oscillator 1 and hold a note to hear the shimmer.

noise.title: Noise
noise.concept: Noise is random hiss rather than a repeating wave. It has no pitch, so it adds breath, grit and percussion.
noise.what: A source of random hiss, white or pink, mixed in with your oscillators.
noise.listenFor: A breathy or airy layer under the notes, with no pitch of its own.
noise.tryThis: Turn off the oscillators' level and play with only noise through a low-pass filter.

filter.title: Filter
filter.concept: A filter removes part of a sound's spectrum. A low-pass keeps the lows and turns the highs down, which makes the sound darker.
filter.what: Turns some frequencies down and lets others through. A low-pass removes harmonics above the cutoff, so the sound gets darker.
filter.listenFor: Hold a note and drag Cutoff down: the brightness drains out.
filter.tryThis: Watch the scope as you do it. The bars on the right go first.

ampEnv.title: Amp envelope
ampEnv.concept: An envelope shapes a note over time. This one controls volume: how it starts, how it settles while held, and how it fades after release.
ampEnv.what: Shapes each note's volume over time in four stages: attack, decay, sustain and release.
ampEnv.listenFor: How a note starts, how it settles while held, and how it fades after you let go.
ampEnv.tryThis: Set Attack to about 500 ms and Release to 2 s, then play slow chords.

filterEnv.title: Filter envelope
filterEnv.concept: This envelope moves the filter cutoff over the life of each note, so the tone changes as the note plays. Plucks and sweeps come from here.
filterEnv.what: Shapes how the filter cutoff moves during each note, in four stages: attack, decay, sustain and release.
filterEnv.listenFor: The tone opening up at the start of a note and closing as it decays.
filterEnv.tryThis: Set Sustain to 0% and Decay to 300 ms, then raise Amount for a pluck.

lfo1.title: LFO 1
lfo1.concept: An LFO is a wave too slow to hear. Instead of making sound, it moves other controls up and down for you. It needs a connection to do anything.
lfo1.what: A slow wave that moves other controls up and down. Connect it from the Connections panel to use it.
lfo1.listenFor: Nothing at first. An LFO only changes the sound once it is connected to something.
lfo1.tryThis: Connect it to Filter cutoff, then change the rate from 0.3 Hz to 6 Hz.

lfo2.title: LFO 2
lfo2.concept: An LFO is a wave too slow to hear. Instead of making sound, it moves other controls up and down for you. It needs a connection to do anything.
lfo2.what: A slow wave that moves other controls up and down. Connect it from the Connections panel to use it.
lfo2.listenFor: Nothing at first. An LFO only changes the sound once it is connected to something.
lfo2.tryThis: Connect it to Filter cutoff, then change the rate from 0.3 Hz to 6 Hz.

amp.title: Amp
amp.concept: The amp stage sets the final loudness of each note. Without an Amp Envelope it is a simple on/off gate.
amp.what: Sets how loud each note is. Without an Amp Envelope, notes switch on with the key and off when you let go, with a 2 ms fade.
amp.listenFor: Notes start and stop abruptly until you add an Amp Envelope.
amp.tryThis: Add an Amp Envelope from the signal chain and hear the difference.

voicing.title: Voicing
voicing.concept: Voicing decides how many notes can sound at once and how the synth behaves when you play them.
voicing.what: Controls how many notes play at once, whether pitch slides between them, and how far the pitch bend moves.
voicing.listenFor: Chords in Poly; single lines in Mono and Legato.
voicing.tryThis: Switch to Mono, set Glide to 200 ms, and play a melody.

output.title: Output
output.concept: The output stage sets the overall volume leaving the synth, after everything else.
output.what: Sets the overall volume after all other modules.
output.listenFor: The whole sound getting louder or quieter, with its tone unchanged.
output.tryThis: Lower it if the sound distorts, or raise it if it is too quiet.

connections.title: Connections
connections.concept: A connection lets one control move another. A source (like an LFO) sends a signal to a destination (like cutoff), scaled by an amount.
connections.what: Eight slots that each link a source to a destination with an amount.
connections.listenFor: The destination moving by itself, in time with the source.
connections.tryThis: Link LFO 1 to Filter cutoff, then drag the amount up and down.

sources.title: Sources
sources.concept: These are things you play with your hands: velocity, mod wheel, aftertouch and the key you press. They can be connected to any destination.
sources.what: Live performance controls: key velocity, mod wheel, aftertouch and key position.
sources.listenFor: Nothing until a connection uses them, then the sound responds to how you play.
sources.tryThis: Connect Mod wheel to Filter cutoff and move the wheel while holding a note.

distortion.title: Distortion
distortion.concept: Distortion squashes and clips the wave, which adds new harmonics. The harder you push it, the grittier it gets. Effects run in order, so distortion before reverb gives a gritty sound in a clean space, while after reverb it also roughens the reverb tail.
distortion.what: Adds grit by pushing the sound hard so the wave flattens and new harmonics appear.
distortion.listenFor: Hold a chord and raise Drive: the sound gets thicker, then buzzier.
distortion.tryThis: Drag it before and after Reverb in the chain and compare how the tail sounds.

chorus.title: Chorus
chorus.concept: Chorus mixes the sound with slightly delayed, slightly detuned copies of itself. The result is wider and thicker. Its order matters: before delay or reverb, the echoes are chorused too; after them, the whole space shimmers.
chorus.what: Thickens and widens the sound with copies that wobble slightly in pitch.
chorus.listenFor: Hold a single note: it sounds like several players at once.
chorus.tryThis: Set Mix to 50% and compare Rate at 0.3 Hz and 4 Hz.

delay.title: Delay
delay.concept: A delay repeats the sound after a gap. Feeding the echoes back in makes them repeat and fade. Order matters: delay before reverb gives echoes that each have their own tail, while reverb before delay repeats the reverb itself.
delay.what: Repeats the sound after a short gap, like an echo.
delay.listenFor: Play a short note and count the echoes as they fade.
delay.tryThis: Turn on Sync, then try 1/8 against 1/4 while playing a steady rhythm.

reverb.title: Reverb
reverb.concept: Reverb adds the many tiny reflections of a room, so the sound seems to happen in a space. It is usually last in the chain, because reverb before distortion gets crushed and roughened by the distortion.
reverb.what: Places the sound in an imaginary room.
reverb.listenFor: Play a short note and listen to the tail after you let go.
reverb.tryThis: Raise Size and Decay together, then add Damping to darken the tail.

control.bypass.title: Bypass (B)
control.bypass.what: Turns this module off without removing it, so you can hear the patch with and without it. Your settings are kept.
control.bypass.listenFor: The sound changes as if the module were not there. Click again and it returns exactly as it was.
control.bypass.tryThis: Hold a note, then click B on the Filter a few times to hear what it adds.

control.solo.title: Solo (S)
control.solo.what: Plays only this source and mutes the other sources. It is for listening to one part of the sound on its own.
control.solo.listenFor: Only this oscillator or noise is left in the mix. The other cards fade to show they are muted.
control.solo.tryThis: With two oscillators playing, solo Oscillator 2 to hear what it adds, then click S again.

control.remove.title: Remove module
control.remove.what: Takes this module out of the patch. Anything connected to it stops moving. Undo brings it back.
control.remove.listenFor: The sound loses whatever this module was adding.
control.remove.tryThis: Remove the Filter, listen, then press Undo at the top to put it back.

control.addModule.title: Add a module
control.addModule.what: Adds another building block to the signal chain: an oscillator, noise, a filter, an envelope or an LFO. The suggested next one is shown first.
control.addModule.listenFor: The patch description under the Explain panel updates, and the sound changes once you play a note.
control.addModule.tryThis: Add the suggested module and hold a note to hear what it changes.

control.handle.title: Modulation handle
control.handle.what: Starts a connection. Drag it onto any knob that shows a ring, or click it and then click a knob, to make that source move the knob automatically.
control.handle.listenFor: The knob you drop it on starts to move by itself, and an arc shows how far it travels.
control.handle.tryThis: Drag the LFO 1 handle onto Filter cutoff, hold a note, then change the amount in the connection list.

control.keyboard.title: Keyboard
control.keyboard.what: Plays notes. Click or drag across the keys, or use the computer keys A to K for white keys and W E T Y U for black keys. C and V lower and raise how hard the notes play.
control.keyboard.listenFor: Keys further right are higher in pitch. Harder (higher velocity) notes are louder.
control.keyboard.tryThis: Play a low key and a high key, then press Z or X to move the whole keyboard an octave.

control.octave.title: Octave shift
control.octave.what: Moves the computer-keyboard keys up or down by an octave. An octave doubles or halves the pitch.
control.octave.listenFor: The same keys now play higher or lower notes. The tone stays the same.
control.octave.tryThis: Click + once, then play the same key you played before.

control.bend.title: Pitch bend wheel
control.bend.what: Slides the pitch of the notes you are holding up or down. It springs back to the middle when you let go. The range is set by Pitch bend range in Voicing.
control.bend.listenFor: The pitch glides smoothly, then returns.
control.bend.tryThis: Hold a note and drag the wheel up, then let go.

control.modWheel.title: Mod wheel
control.modWheel.what: A live control you move by hand. It does nothing until you connect it to a knob. Connect it with the Mod wheel handle under Sources.
control.modWheel.listenFor: Nothing at first. Once connected, the destination knob follows the wheel.
control.modWheel.tryThis: Connect Mod wheel to Filter cutoff, hold a note and drag the wheel.

control.scopeMode.title: Scope display
control.scopeMode.what: Chooses how the scope draws the sound. Wave shows the shape of the sound over time. Spectrum shows how much of each pitch is in it.
control.scopeMode.listenFor: A bright sound has tall bars far to the right in Spectrum. A dull one has bars only on the left.
control.scopeMode.tryThis: Hold a note on a saw wave and switch between Wave and Spectrum.

control.scopeTap.title: Scope tap
control.scopeTap.what: Chooses where in the signal path the scope listens: right after the oscillators, after the filter, or at the final output. Changing it does not change the sound.
control.scopeTap.listenFor: Compare Osc and Filter in Spectrum: the filter removes the high bars above its cutoff.
control.scopeTap.tryThis: Set the tap to Osc, hold a note, then switch to Filter and close the cutoff.

control.meter.title: Output level
control.meter.what: Shows how loud the synth is at its output. If it reaches the top the sound is too loud and may distort.
control.meter.listenFor: The bar rises with louder notes and chords.
control.meter.tryThis: Play a chord and lower Volume in Output if the meter hits the top.

control.newPatch.title: New patch
control.newPatch.what: Starts again from a single saw oscillator. Your current patch is replaced, and Undo can bring it back.
control.newPatch.listenFor: The synth goes back to one oscillator and nothing else.
control.newPatch.tryThis: Click it, then build up again: add a filter, an envelope or a second oscillator.

control.undo.title: Undo
control.undo.what: Reverses your last change to the patch, such as a knob move, adding a module or a new connection.
control.undo.listenFor: The control and the sound go back to how they were.
control.undo.tryThis: Turn a knob a long way, then click Undo.

control.redo.title: Redo
control.redo.what: Brings back a change you just undid.
control.redo.listenFor: The control and the sound return to the change.

control.settings.title: Audio and MIDI settings
control.settings.what: Opens the dialog where you choose the audio output device and which MIDI keyboards can play the synth.
control.settings.listenFor: With the right output chosen you hear sound. With a MIDI input enabled, your keyboard plays the synth.
control.settings.tryThis: Open it, enable your MIDI keyboard, then play it.

control.limiter.title: Limiter
control.limiter.what: A safety limiter that is always on at the very end. It stops the output going above -0.3 dBFS, so loud patches do not clip. It is the only processing you cannot switch off.
control.limiter.listenFor: The light comes on when the limiter is working. A flicker on peaks is fine; staying lit means the patch is too loud.
control.limiter.tryThis: Play a big chord with Filter resonance at 100% and watch the light, then lower Volume.

control.effectGrip.title: Effect order
control.effectGrip.what: Drag this handle to move an effect earlier or later in the chain. Sound passes through the effects from left to right.
control.effectGrip.listenFor: The same effects sound different in a different order. Reverb then distortion is rougher than distortion then reverb.
control.effectGrip.tryThis: Drag Distortion from before Reverb to after it while holding a chord.

control.oscMore.title: More
control.oscMore.what: Opens the oscillator's extra row: unison, hard sync, anti-aliasing, and for Oscillator 1, ring modulation and FM.
control.oscMore.listenFor: Nothing changes by opening it. The controls inside do the work.
control.oscMore.tryThis: Open it on Oscillator 2 and try Sync.

osc1.enabled.title: Oscillator 1
osc1.enabled.what: Shows whether Oscillator 1 is in your patch. Add or remove it from the signal chain.
osc1.enabled.listenFor: When it is present, you hear it in the mix.
osc1.enabled.tryThis: Click Oscillator in the signal chain to add or remove it.

osc1.wave.title: Wave
osc1.wave.what: Chooses the wave shape: Sine, Triangle, Saw or Pulse. The shape sets the tone.
osc1.wave.listenFor: Sine is pure, Triangle mellow, Saw bright and buzzy, Pulse hollow.
osc1.wave.tryThis: Hold a note and click through all four waves.

osc1.octave.title: Octave
osc1.octave.what: Shifts the pitch by whole octaves, from -2 to +2. Each octave doubles or halves the frequency.
osc1.octave.listenFor: The same note sounding higher or lower.
osc1.octave.tryThis: Set -1 for a bass layer, then +1 for a bright one.

osc1.semitone.title: Semitone
osc1.semitone.what: Shifts the pitch in semitones, from -12 to +12. Twelve semitones make an octave.
osc1.semitone.listenFor: Small steps up or down; +7 gives a fifth, +12 an octave.
osc1.semitone.tryThis: Set +7 on a held note for a power-chord sound.

osc1.fine.title: Fine
osc1.fine.what: Shifts the pitch by up to 100 cents either way. 100 cents is one semitone.
osc1.fine.listenFor: A slow, shimmering beat when two oscillators are slightly apart.
osc1.fine.tryThis: Set +8 cents on a held note, then raise it until it sounds out of tune.

osc1.pulseWidth.title: Pulse width
osc1.pulseWidth.what: Sets how wide the Pulse wave's high part is, from 5% to 95%. It only affects the Pulse wave.
osc1.pulseWidth.listenFor: 50% sounds hollow; narrow settings sound thin and nasal.
osc1.pulseWidth.tryThis: Choose Pulse, then sweep from 50% down to 10%.

osc1.level.title: Level
osc1.level.what: Sets how loud Oscillator 1 is in the mix, from silence (−∞ dB) up to 0 dB.
osc1.level.listenFor: This oscillator getting louder or quieter against the others.
osc1.level.tryThis: Balance it against the others until nothing sounds buried.

osc1.phaseReset.title: Phase reset
osc1.phaseReset.what: When on, the wave restarts from the same point on every note. When off, it keeps running.
osc1.phaseReset.listenFor: On: every note starts the same. Off: slight variation between notes.
osc1.phaseReset.tryThis: Turn it off, then play the same note repeatedly.

osc1.bypass.title: Bypass
osc1.bypass.what: Passes the signal through Oscillator 1 untouched, so you can compare with and without it.
osc1.bypass.listenFor: The sound with this module taken out of the picture.
osc1.bypass.tryThis: Toggle it while holding a note to A/B the effect.

osc1.solo.title: Solo
osc1.solo.what: Mutes the other sources so you hear only Oscillator 1.
osc1.solo.listenFor: Only this oscillator, without the rest of the mix.
osc1.solo.tryThis: Solo it to hear its wave on its own, then switch off.

osc2.enabled.title: Oscillator 2
osc2.enabled.what: Shows whether Oscillator 2 is in your patch. Add or remove it from the signal chain.
osc2.enabled.listenFor: When it is present, you hear it in the mix.
osc2.enabled.tryThis: Click Oscillator in the signal chain to add or remove it.

osc2.wave.title: Wave
osc2.wave.what: Chooses the wave shape: Sine, Triangle, Saw or Pulse. The shape sets the tone.
osc2.wave.listenFor: Sine is pure, Triangle mellow, Saw bright and buzzy, Pulse hollow.
osc2.wave.tryThis: Hold a note and click through all four waves.

osc2.octave.title: Octave

osc2.octave.listenFor: The same note sounding higher or lower.
osc2.octave.tryThis: Set -1 for a bass layer, then +1 for a bright one. Compare it against Oscillator 1.

osc2.semitone.title: Semitone
osc2.semitone.what: Shifts the pitch in semitones, from -12 to +12. Twelve semitones make an octave.
osc2.semitone.listenFor: Small steps up or down; +7 gives a fifth, +12 an octave.
osc2.semitone.tryThis: Set +7 on a held note for a power-chord sound. Compare it against Oscillator 1.

osc2.fine.title: Fine
osc2.fine.what: Shifts the pitch by up to 100 cents either way. 100 cents is one semitone. Use it to detune against Oscillator 1.
osc2.fine.listenFor: A slow, shimmering beat when two oscillators are slightly apart.
osc2.fine.tryThis: Set +8 cents on a held note, then raise it until it sounds out of tune.

osc2.pulseWidth.title: Pulse width
osc2.pulseWidth.what: Sets how wide the Pulse wave's high part is, from 5% to 95%. It only affects the Pulse wave.
osc2.pulseWidth.listenFor: 50% sounds hollow; narrow settings sound thin and nasal.
osc2.pulseWidth.tryThis: Choose Pulse, then sweep from 50% down to 10%.

osc2.level.title: Level
osc2.level.what: Sets how loud Oscillator 2 is in the mix, from silence (−∞ dB) up to 0 dB.
osc2.level.listenFor: This oscillator getting louder or quieter against the others.
osc2.level.tryThis: Balance it against the others until nothing sounds buried.

osc2.phaseReset.title: Phase reset
osc2.phaseReset.what: When on, the wave restarts from the same point on every note. When off, it keeps running.
osc2.phaseReset.listenFor: On: every note starts the same. Off: slight variation between notes.
osc2.phaseReset.tryThis: Turn it off, then play the same note repeatedly.

osc2.bypass.title: Bypass
osc2.bypass.what: Passes the signal through Oscillator 2 untouched, so you can compare with and without it.
osc2.bypass.listenFor: The sound with this module taken out of the picture.
osc2.bypass.tryThis: Toggle it while holding a note to A/B the effect.

osc2.solo.title: Solo
osc2.solo.what: Mutes the other sources so you hear only Oscillator 2.
osc2.solo.listenFor: Only this oscillator, without the rest of the mix.
osc2.solo.tryThis: Solo it to hear its wave on its own, then switch off.

osc3.enabled.title: Oscillator 3
osc3.enabled.what: Shows whether Oscillator 3 is in your patch. Add or remove it from the signal chain.
osc3.enabled.listenFor: When it is present, you hear it in the mix.
osc3.enabled.tryThis: Click Oscillator in the signal chain to add or remove it.

osc3.wave.listenFor: Sine is pure, Triangle mellow, Saw bright and buzzy, Pulse hollow.

osc3.semitone.title: Semitone
osc3.semitone.what: Shifts the pitch in semitones, from -12 to +12. Twelve semitones make an octave.
osc3.semitone.listenFor: Small steps up or down; +7 gives a fifth, +12 an octave.
osc3.semitone.tryThis: Set +7 on a held note for a power-chord sound. Compare it against Oscillator 1.

osc3.fine.what: Shifts the pitch by up to 100 cents either way. 100 cents is one semitone. Use it to detune against Oscillator 1.
osc3.fine.listenFor: A slow, shimmering beat when two oscillators are slightly apart.
osc3.fine.tryThis: Set +8 cents on a held note, then raise it until it sounds out of tune.

osc3.pulseWidth.title: Pulse width
osc3.pulseWidth.what: Sets how wide the Pulse wave's high part is, from 5% to 95%. It only affects the Pulse wave.
osc3.pulseWidth.listenFor: 50% sounds hollow; narrow settings sound thin and nasal.
osc3.pulseWidth.tryThis: Choose Pulse, then sweep from 50% down to 10%.

osc3.level.title: Level
osc3.level.what: Sets how loud Oscillator 3 is in the mix, from silence (−∞ dB) up to 0 dB.
osc3.level.listenFor: This oscillator getting louder or quieter against the others.
osc3.level.tryThis: Balance it against the others until nothing sounds buried.

osc3.phaseReset.title: Phase reset
osc3.phaseReset.what: When on, the wave restarts from the same point on every note. When off, it keeps running.
osc3.phaseReset.listenFor: On: every note starts the same. Off: slight variation between notes.
osc3.phaseReset.tryThis: Turn it off, then play the same note repeatedly.

osc3.bypass.title: Bypass
osc3.bypass.what: Passes the signal through Oscillator 3 untouched, so you can compare with and without it.
osc3.bypass.listenFor: The sound with this module taken out of the picture.
osc3.bypass.tryThis: Toggle it while holding a note to A/B the effect.

osc3.solo.title: Solo
osc3.solo.what: Mutes the other sources so you hear only Oscillator 3.
osc3.solo.listenFor: Only this oscillator, without the rest of the mix.
osc3.solo.tryThis: Solo it to hear its wave on its own, then switch off.

noise.enabled.title: Noise
noise.enabled.what: Shows whether Noise is in your patch. Add or remove it from the signal chain.
noise.enabled.listenFor: When present, a hiss joins the mix.
noise.enabled.tryThis: Click Noise in the signal chain to add it.

noise.colour.title: Colour
noise.colour.what: Chooses White noise (bright, like static) or Pink noise (softer, with fewer highs).
noise.colour.listenFor: White hisses like steam; pink rumbles more like rain.
noise.colour.tryThis: Switch between White and Pink while holding a note.

noise.level.title: Level
noise.level.what: Sets how loud the noise is in the mix, from silence up to 0 dB. It starts at -18 dB.
noise.level.listenFor: A little noise adds breath; a lot hides the pitched sound.
noise.level.tryThis: Add a touch, then sweep Filter cutoff down.

noise.bypass.title: Bypass
noise.bypass.what: Passes the signal through Noise untouched, so you can compare with and without it.
noise.bypass.listenFor: The sound with this module taken out of the picture.
noise.bypass.tryThis: Toggle it while holding a note to A/B the effect.

noise.solo.title: Solo
noise.solo.what: Mutes the other sources so you hear only Noise.
noise.solo.listenFor: Just the hiss on its own.
noise.solo.tryThis: Solo it, then change the colour.

filter.enabled.title: Filter
filter.enabled.what: Shows whether the Filter is in your patch. Add or remove it from the signal chain.
filter.enabled.listenFor: With it present, you can darken or thin the sound.
filter.enabled.tryThis: Click Filter in the signal chain to add it.

filter.mode.title: Mode
filter.mode.what: LP keeps lows and removes highs, HP does the opposite, BP keeps a band. 24 dB slopes cut more steeply than 12 dB.
filter.mode.listenFor: HP thins the sound out; BP sounds like it is coming through a phone.
filter.mode.tryThis: Hold a note and click through the four modes.

filter.cutoff.title: Cutoff
filter.cutoff.what: Sets where the filter starts cutting, from 20 Hz to 20 kHz. Harmonics beyond it are turned down.
filter.cutoff.listenFor: Lower it and the note gets darker, as if it moved behind a door.
filter.cutoff.tryThis: Hold a chord and sweep from 20 kHz to 200 Hz.

filter.resonance.title: Resonance
filter.resonance.what: Boosts frequencies right at the cutoff, adding a peak. It runs from 0% to 100%.
filter.resonance.listenFor: A whistling, vocal edge that follows the cutoff.
filter.resonance.tryThis: Set it near 80% and sweep Cutoff slowly.

filter.keyTracking.title: Key tracking
filter.keyTracking.what: Makes the cutoff follow the note you play. At 100%, it moves in step with the pitch.
filter.keyTracking.listenFor: Higher notes stay as bright as low ones.
filter.keyTracking.tryThis: Set it to 100%, then play low and high notes.

filter.drive.title: Drive
filter.drive.what: Pushes the signal harder into the filter, from 0 to 24 dB. It adds warmth and gentle distortion.
filter.drive.listenFor: A thicker, grittier tone as it rises.
filter.drive.tryThis: Raise it to 12 dB while holding a chord.

filter.bypass.title: Bypass
filter.bypass.what: Passes the signal through the Filter untouched, so you can compare with and without it.
filter.bypass.tryThis: Toggle it while holding a note to A/B the effect.

ampEnv.enabled.title: Amp envelope
ampEnv.enabled.what: Shows whether the Amp Envelope is in your patch. Add or remove it from the signal chain.
ampEnv.enabled.listenFor: With it present, notes change over time. Without it, notes are on or off.
ampEnv.enabled.tryThis: Click Amp Envelope in the signal chain to add it.

ampEnv.attack.title: Attack
ampEnv.attack.what: How long the volume takes to reach its peak after you press a key, from 1 ms to 10 s.
ampEnv.attack.listenFor: Short attacks pluck; long ones swell in.
ampEnv.attack.tryThis: Repeat one note while you sweep from 1 ms to 1 s.

ampEnv.decay.title: Decay
ampEnv.decay.what: How long the volume takes to fall from its peak to the sustain level, from 1 ms to 10 s.
ampEnv.decay.listenFor: Only audible when Sustain is below 100%.
ampEnv.decay.tryThis: Set Sustain to 0% and Decay to 200 ms for a pluck.

ampEnv.sustain.title: Sustain
ampEnv.sustain.what: The volume level held while the key stays down, from 0% to 100%. It is a level, not a time.
ampEnv.sustain.listenFor: At 0% the note dies away even while you hold it.
ampEnv.sustain.tryThis: Hold a key and drag Sustain down slowly.

ampEnv.release.title: Release
ampEnv.release.what: How long the volume takes to fall to nothing after you let go, up to 20 s.
ampEnv.release.listenFor: Long releases make notes overlap and blur together.
ampEnv.release.tryThis: Set it to 3 s and play short, separate notes.

ampEnv.bypass.title: Bypass
ampEnv.bypass.what: Passes the signal through the Amp Envelope untouched, so you can compare with and without it.
ampEnv.bypass.listenFor: The sound with this envelope taken out of the picture.
ampEnv.bypass.tryThis: Toggle it while holding a note to A/B the effect.

filterEnv.enabled.title: Filter envelope
filterEnv.enabled.what: Shows whether the Filter Envelope is in your patch. Add or remove it from the signal chain.
filterEnv.enabled.listenFor: With it present, notes change over time.
filterEnv.enabled.tryThis: Click Filter Envelope in the signal chain to add it.

filterEnv.attack.title: Attack
filterEnv.attack.what: How long the cutoff takes to reach its peak after you press a key, from 1 ms to 10 s.
filterEnv.attack.listenFor: Short attacks pluck; long ones swell in.
filterEnv.attack.tryThis: Repeat one note while you sweep from 1 ms to 1 s.

filterEnv.decay.title: Decay
filterEnv.decay.what: How long the cutoff takes to fall from its peak to the sustain level, from 1 ms to 10 s.
filterEnv.decay.listenFor: Only audible when Sustain is below 100%.
filterEnv.decay.tryThis: Set Sustain to 0% and Decay to 200 ms for a pluck.

filterEnv.sustain.title: Sustain
filterEnv.sustain.what: The cutoff level held while the key stays down, from 0% to 100%. It is a level, not a time.
filterEnv.sustain.listenFor: At 0% the note dies away even while you hold it.
filterEnv.sustain.tryThis: Hold a key and drag Sustain down slowly.

filterEnv.release.title: Release
filterEnv.release.what: How long the cutoff takes to fall to nothing after you let go, up to 20 s.
filterEnv.release.listenFor: Long releases make notes overlap and blur together.
filterEnv.release.tryThis: Set it to 3 s and play short, separate notes.

filterEnv.bypass.title: Bypass
filterEnv.bypass.what: Passes the signal through the Filter Envelope untouched, so you can compare with and without it.
filterEnv.bypass.listenFor: The sound with this envelope taken out of the picture.
filterEnv.bypass.tryThis: Toggle it while holding a note to A/B the effect.

ampEnv.velocitySens.title: Velocity sensitivity
ampEnv.velocitySens.what: How much key velocity changes the volume. At 0% every note is equally loud; at 100% soft presses are quiet.
ampEnv.velocitySens.tryThis: Set it to 100% and play soft, then hard.

filterEnv.amount.title: Amount
filterEnv.amount.what: How far the envelope moves the cutoff, from -100% to 100%. Negative values move it down instead.
filterEnv.amount.listenFor: A bigger sweep as it rises; a downward sweep when negative.
filterEnv.amount.tryThis: Set Cutoff low, Amount to 80%, and Decay to 400 ms.

lfo1.enabled.title: LFO 1
lfo1.enabled.what: Shows whether LFO 1 is in your patch. Add or remove it from the signal chain.
lfo1.enabled.listenFor: Once present, it can be used as a source in Connections.
lfo1.enabled.tryThis: Add LFO 1, then link it in Connections.

lfo1.shape.title: Shape
lfo1.shape.what: The wave the LFO follows: Sine, Triangle, Saw up, Saw down, Square or Sample & hold.
lfo1.shape.listenFor: Sine is smooth, Square jumps, Sample & hold is random steps.
lfo1.shape.tryThis: Send it to cutoff and cycle through the shapes.

lfo1.rate.title: Rate
lfo1.rate.what: How many times a second the LFO repeats, from 0.01 Hz to 50 Hz.
lfo1.rate.listenFor: Slow rates sweep; fast rates wobble, then buzz.
lfo1.rate.tryThis: Try 0.3 Hz, then 6 Hz, on Filter cutoff.

lfo1.retrigger.title: Retrigger
lfo1.retrigger.what: When on, the LFO restarts from the beginning on every note. When off, it runs freely.
lfo1.retrigger.listenFor: On: every note moves the same way. Off: each starts at a different point.
lfo1.retrigger.tryThis: Turn it on and play the same note repeatedly.

lfo1.fade.title: Fade-in
lfo1.fade.what: How long the LFO takes to reach full strength after a note starts, up to 5 s. Off means immediate.
lfo1.fade.listenFor: Vibrato that starts after a short delay.
lfo1.fade.tryThis: Send it to pitch, set Fade to 1 s, and hold a note.

lfo1.bypass.title: Bypass
lfo1.bypass.what: Passes the signal through LFO 1 untouched, so you can compare with and without it.
lfo1.bypass.listenFor: The sound with this LFO's motion taken out.
lfo1.bypass.tryThis: Toggle it while holding a note to A/B the effect.

lfo2.enabled.title: LFO 2
lfo2.enabled.what: Shows whether LFO 2 is in your patch. Add or remove it from the signal chain.
lfo2.enabled.listenFor: Once present, it can be used as a source in Connections.
lfo2.enabled.tryThis: Add LFO 2, then link it in Connections.

lfo2.rate.tryThis: Try 0.3 Hz, then 6 Hz, on Filter cutoff.

mod1.source.title: Source
mod1.source.what: Chooses what drives this connection: an LFO, envelope, velocity, mod wheel, aftertouch or key.
mod1.source.listenFor: Nothing until you also choose a destination.
mod1.source.tryThis: Choose LFO 1 as the source, then pick a destination.

mod1.dest.title: Destination
mod1.dest.what: Chooses what the source moves, such as pitch, pulse width, cutoff, resonance, level, pan or LFO rate.
mod1.dest.listenFor: The chosen control moving by itself.
mod1.dest.tryThis: Choose Filter cutoff and listen to the tone move.

mod1.amount.title: Amount
mod1.amount.what: How far the source moves the destination, -100% to +100%. At 100%: pitch 2 semitones, cutoff 6 octaves, pulse width 45 points, LFO rate 3 octaves.
mod1.amount.listenFor: Negative values flip the movement. On level, -100% is silent and +100% doubles; on pan, it reaches hard left or right.
mod1.amount.tryThis: Start at +50%, then try -50%. On resonance, 100% covers the whole range.

voicing.mode.title: Voice mode
voicing.mode.what: Poly plays chords. Mono plays one note at a time. Legato is mono, but joined notes do not restart envelopes.
voicing.mode.listenFor: Poly sounds full; Mono and Legato suit leads and basses.
voicing.mode.tryThis: Switch to Legato and play overlapping notes.

voicing.voices.title: Voices
voicing.voices.what: The most notes that can sound at once, from 1 to 16. A new note beyond that takes a voice that has been let go, or else the oldest held one.
voicing.voices.listenFor: Older notes cutting off when you play too many.
voicing.voices.tryThis: Set it to 2 and play a three-note chord.

voicing.glide.title: Glide
voicing.glide.what: How long pitch takes to slide from one note to the next, up to 2 s. Off jumps straight.
voicing.glide.tryThis: Set Mono mode, Glide to 300 ms, and play two notes.

voicing.bendRange.title: Pitch bend range
voicing.bendRange.what: How far the pitch bend wheel moves the pitch, from 1 to 24 semitones either way.
voicing.bendRange.listenFor: Wider settings bend further for the same wheel move.
voicing.bendRange.tryThis: Set it to 12, then move the pitch wheel fully.

output.volume.title: Volume
output.volume.what: Sets the overall output level, from silence up to +6 dB. 0 dB leaves it unchanged.
output.volume.listenFor: The whole sound louder or quieter, tone unchanged.
output.volume.tryThis: Lower it if loud chords distort.

osc1.unison.title: Unison
osc1.unison.what: Stacks up to 7 copies of Oscillator 1 on top of each other, each slightly out of tune. 1 means a single copy.
osc1.unison.listenFor: More copies sound wider and thicker, with a slow shimmer between them.
osc1.unison.tryThis: Hold a chord and raise it from 1 to 5.

osc1.unisonDetune.title: Unison detune
osc1.unisonDetune.what: How far apart the unison copies are tuned, from 0 to 100 cents. It does nothing with one copy.
osc1.unisonDetune.listenFor: Small amounts shimmer. Large amounts sound out of tune.
osc1.unisonDetune.tryThis: Set Unison to 5, then sweep this from 5 to 60 cents.

osc1.unisonSpread.title: Unison spread
osc1.unisonSpread.what: How far the unison copies are placed across the left and right speakers, from 0 to 100%.
osc1.unisonSpread.listenFor: At 0% everything sits in the middle. At 100% the sound opens out wide.
osc1.unisonSpread.tryThis: Use headphones, set Unison to 5 and move this from 0% to 100%.

osc1.antiAlias.title: Anti-aliasing
osc1.antiAlias.what: Keeps Oscillator 1 free of aliasing. Switch it off to hear the harsh, whistling sound a naive digital wave makes.
osc1.antiAlias.listenFor: Off: inharmonic whistles that get worse on high notes. On: clean.
osc1.antiAlias.tryThis: Play high notes on a saw, then toggle it.

osc2.unison.title: Unison
osc2.unison.what: Stacks up to 7 copies of Oscillator 2 on top of each other, each slightly out of tune. 1 means a single copy.
osc2.unison.listenFor: More copies sound wider and thicker, with a slow shimmer between them.
osc2.unison.tryThis: Hold a chord and raise it from 1 to 5.

osc2.unisonDetune.title: Unison detune

osc2.unisonSpread.tryThis: Use headphones, set Unison to 5 and move this from 0% to 100%.

osc2.antiAlias.title: Anti-aliasing

osc3.unison.listenFor: More copies sound wider and thicker, with a slow shimmer between them.

osc2.sync.title: Hard sync
osc2.sync.what: Restarts Oscillator 2 every time Oscillator 1 restarts its cycle. Oscillator 1 is the master.
osc2.sync.listenFor: The pitch of Oscillator 1 stays, but the tone changes. Move the synced oscillator's pitch for a tearing sweep.
osc2.sync.tryThis: Turn it on, then sweep Oscillator 2's semitone or fine up and down.

osc3.sync.title: Hard sync
osc3.sync.what: Restarts Oscillator 3 every time Oscillator 1 restarts its cycle. Oscillator 1 is the master.
osc3.sync.listenFor: The pitch of Oscillator 1 stays, but the tone changes. Move the synced oscillator's pitch for a tearing sweep.
osc3.sync.tryThis: Turn it on, then sweep Oscillator 3's semitone or fine up and down.

ring.level.title: Ring modulation level
ring.level.what: Mixes in Oscillator 1 multiplied by Oscillator 2, from -60 dB (off) to 0 dB. The result contains the sum and difference of their frequencies.
ring.level.listenFor: Clangy, bell-like tones that are not tuned to either note.
ring.level.tryThis: Raise it to -12 dB, then detune Oscillator 2 by a few semitones.

fm.amount.title: FM amount
fm.amount.what: How strongly Oscillator 1 modulates the pitch of the target, from 0 to 100%. Oscillator 1 is the modulator and the target is the carrier.
fm.amount.listenFor: Higher amounts add more sidebands, so the tone gets brighter and harsher.
fm.amount.tryThis: Raise it slowly, then change the target's octave or semitone to move the sidebands.

fm.target.title: FM target
fm.target.what: Chooses which oscillator Oscillator 1 modulates: Osc 2, Osc 3 or both.
fm.target.listenFor: The target's frequency ratio to Oscillator 1 decides the sidebands. Whole-number ratios sound tuned; others sound clangy.
fm.target.tryThis: Set the amount to 30%, then switch between Osc 2 and Both.

distortion.drive.title: Drive
distortion.drive.what: How hard the signal is pushed into the distortion, from 0 to 40 dB.
distortion.drive.listenFor: More drive means more grit and more harmonics.
distortion.drive.tryThis: Hold a chord and raise it to 24 dB.

distortion.tone.title: Tone
distortion.tone.what: A tilt from dark to bright for the distorted sound.
distortion.tone.listenFor: Low: soft and muffled. High: fizzy and sharp.
distortion.tone.tryThis: Set drive high, then sweep Tone.

distortion.mix.title: Mix
distortion.mix.what: How much distorted sound is blended with the original, from 0 to 100%.
distortion.mix.listenFor: Lower values keep the clean sound and add edge.

chorus.rate.title: Rate
chorus.rate.what: How fast the chorus's internal wobble moves, from 0.1 to 8 Hz.
chorus.rate.listenFor: Slow: gentle drift. Fast: a warbling vibrato.

chorus.depth.title: Depth
chorus.depth.what: How far the chorus bends the pitch of its copies, from 0 to 100%.
chorus.depth.listenFor: More depth sounds wider and more seasick.
chorus.depth.tryThis: Hold a note and raise it from 20% to 80%.

chorus.mix.title: Mix
chorus.mix.what: How much chorused sound is blended with the original, from 0 to 100%.
chorus.mix.listenFor: At 0% nothing changes. Around 50% the sound thickens.

delay.time.title: Time
delay.time.what: The gap before each echo, from 1 to 2000 ms. It is ignored while Sync is on.
delay.time.listenFor: Short times thicken; long times give separate echoes.
delay.time.tryThis: Play a short note, then try 150 ms and 600 ms.

delay.sync.title: Sync
delay.sync.what: Locks the echo time to the tempo, using the division instead of Time.
delay.sync.listenFor: The echoes land on the beat and follow the tempo.

delay.division.title: Division
delay.division.what: The note length of each echo while Sync is on, such as 1/4 or 1/8.
delay.division.listenFor: Shorter divisions give faster, busier echoes.
delay.division.tryThis: Switch from 1/4 to 1/8 while holding a rhythm.

delay.feedback.title: Feedback
delay.feedback.what: How much of each echo is fed back in to make the next one, from 0 to 95%.
delay.feedback.listenFor: Low: one or two echoes. High: a long trail that fades slowly.

delay.pingPong.title: Ping-pong
delay.pingPong.what: Bounces the echoes between the left and right speakers.
delay.pingPong.listenFor: Echoes alternate from side to side.
delay.pingPong.tryThis: Turn it on with headphones and a short note.

delay.mix.title: Mix
delay.mix.what: How much echo is blended with the original, from 0 to 100%.
delay.mix.listenFor: At 0% there is no echo. Higher values make the echoes louder.

reverb.size.title: Size
reverb.size.what: The size of the imaginary room, from 0 to 100%.
reverb.size.listenFor: Small: a tight booth. Large: a hall.
reverb.size.tryThis: Play a short note and raise it from 10% to 90%.

reverb.decay.title: Decay
reverb.decay.what: How long the reverb tail takes to fade, from 0.2 to 10 seconds.
reverb.decay.listenFor: Short: quick ambience. Long: a wash that hangs after you let go.
reverb.decay.tryThis: Play a short note and try 1 s, then 8 s.

reverb.damping.title: Damping
reverb.damping.what: How quickly the reverb loses its high frequencies as it fades, from 0 to 100%.
reverb.damping.listenFor: More damping gives a darker, softer tail.
reverb.damping.tryThis: Set a long decay, then raise damping.

reverb.mix.title: Mix
reverb.mix.what: How much reverb is blended with the original, from 0 to 100%.
reverb.mix.listenFor: At 0% the sound is dry. Higher values push it further away.

lfo1.sync.title: Sync
lfo1.sync.what: Locks LFO 1 to the tempo, using the division instead of Rate.
lfo1.sync.listenFor: The movement stays in time with the beat.
lfo1.sync.tryThis: Connect it to Filter cutoff, turn Sync on and choose 1/4.

lfo1.division.title: Division
lfo1.division.what: The note length of one LFO 1 cycle while Sync is on, such as 1/4 or 1/8.
lfo1.division.listenFor: Longer divisions sweep slowly; shorter ones pulse faster.
lfo1.division.tryThis: Switch between 1/4 and 1/16 on a filter sweep.

lfo2.sync.title: Sync
lfo2.sync.what: Locks LFO 2 to the tempo, using the division instead of Rate.
lfo2.sync.listenFor: The movement stays in time with the beat.
lfo2.sync.tryThis: Connect it to Filter cutoff, turn Sync on and choose 1/4.

lfo2.division.title: Division
lfo2.division.what: The note length of one LFO 2 cycle while Sync is on, such as 1/4 or 1/8.
lfo2.division.listenFor: Longer divisions sweep slowly; shorter ones pulse faster.
lfo2.division.tryThis: Switch between 1/4 and 1/16 on a filter sweep.
